520: I lean in close and whisper wisdom. Most of it is 'perhaps we should wait and see.'
521: I advise the crown on grave matters. This morning the grave matter was the breakfast menu.
522: I say things slowly and importantly. It makes the smallest suggestion sound enormous.
523: My advice is always the same: proceed with caution. I have built a whole career on it.
524: I whisper into royal ears. Half of what I whisper is simply 'that is a wise question.'
525: A councillor must look thoughtful at all times. I furrow my brow even when I am only hungry.

527: I nod gravely, stroke my chin, and say 'indeed.' That is roughly ninety percent of the job.
528: They pay me to have opinions. I have learned to have them very, very slowly.
529: My counsel is priceless. It is also, if I am honest, mostly 'let us not be hasty.'
530: I stand near the throne and murmur. The murmuring is the important part, apparently.
531: I advised the king to wait until morning before deciding. It is my finest and most frequent advice.
532: I speak in a low, wise voice. Even 'good morning' sounds like a warning when I say it.
533: Grand titles, grand robes, grand whispers. The whispers usually mean 'ask someone else.'
534: I am consulted on everything. My answer to everything is a long, meaningful pause.
535: A councillor never rushes. I have kept the whole court waiting on a single word for an hour.

538: I have advised three kings. Each one, in the end, did the opposite. I remain very proud.
539: My whole role is to look wise and lean in close. The leaning is surprisingly tiring.
540: I watch numbers go up and down all day. Today they went down, then up, then it was lunch.
541: My job is to stare at the numbers until they mean something. I am patient. The numbers are more patient.
542: The numbers rose. Then they fell. I wrote down that they did both. That is the whole report.
543: I study patterns for a living. Today's pattern was that I got hungry at exactly the same time.
544: A number went up. I felt joy. It came back down. I felt informed.
545: I watch the figures so closely that when they blink, I blink too. They do not blink.
546: My conclusion, after hours of careful study, is that the numbers are up. Also that they are down.
547: I turn columns of numbers into meaning. Today the meaning was 'perhaps have a sandwich.'

549: I have looked at these numbers so long I have started to root for a few of them.

552: My whole trade is watching things rise and fall. Today, mostly, it was my own attention.
553: The figures wobbled all morning. I wrote 'the figures wobbled.' It is a strong report.
